## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works describe a kinship between Qarun and Musa, give the source of his wealth, and give other names for him.
- Hadith to add later: reports about Qarun, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Qarun and his wealth  (`#qarun-and-his-wealth`)

Cited ayat: 28:76-78

> **28:76** إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ لَا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْفَرِحِينَ
>
> **28:77** وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَأَحْسِن كَمَآ أَحْسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ وَلَا تَبْغِ ٱلْفَسَادَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
>
> **28:78** قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِىٓ أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُ قُوَّةً وَأَكْثَرُ جَمْعًا وَلَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:76): Qarun was of the people of Musa, and he oppressed them, and God had given him treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men.

**c2** (28:76): His people told him not to exult, for God does not love the exultant.

**c3** (28:77): They told him to seek, in what God had given him, the home of the Hereafter, not to forget his share of this world, to do good as God had done good to him, and not to seek corruption in the land, for God does not love the corrupters.

**c4** (28:78): He said that he had been given it only because of knowledge that he had, and the ayah asks whether he did not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him and had gathered more, and that the guilty are not asked about their sins.

### One-minute summary

Qarun was of the people of Musa, and God had given him treasures [c1]. His people told him not to exult and to seek the home of the Hereafter in what God had given him [c2][c3]. He said that he had been given it because of knowledge that he had [c4].

### Complete story

Qarun was of the people of Musa, and he oppressed them, and God had given him treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men [c1]. His people told him not to exult, for God does not love the exultant [c2]. They told him to seek, in what God had given him, the home of the Hereafter, not to forget his share of this world, to do good as God had done good to him, and not to seek corruption in the land, for God does not love the corrupters [c3]. He said that he had been given it only because of knowledge that he had, and the ayah asks whether he did not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him and had gathered more, and that the guilty are not asked about their sins [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat give his people's counsel as a warning against exulting and a call to seek the Hereafter without forgetting his share of this world [c2][c3]. The knowledge he claims is not described [c4].

### Kids mode

Qarun had been given great treasures by God [c1]. His people told him not to exult [c2]. He said that he had been given them because of knowledge that he had [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets his people's counsel beside his answer that his wealth came from his own knowledge [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how much wealth he had, or how he came by it.
- Not established: how he was related to the people of Musa, beyond the words that he was of them.
- Not established: what knowledge he claimed.

## 2. His display and his end  (`#his-display-and-his-end`)

Cited ayat: 28:79-82

> **28:79** فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فِى زِينَتِهِۦ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا يَٰلَيْتَ لَنَا مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ
>
> **28:80** وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ وَيْلَكُمْ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِّمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ
>
> **28:81** فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةٍ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنتَصِرِينَ
>
> **28:82** وَأَصْبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوْا۟ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيْكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقْدِرُ لَوْلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَا وَيْكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:79): He came out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted the life of this world said that they wished they had what Qarun had been given, for he was possessor of a great fortune.

**c2** (28:80): Those who had been given knowledge said, woe to you, the reward of God is better for one who believes and does good, and none will attain it except the patient.

**c3** (28:81): God made the earth swallow him and his house, and he had no group to help him other than God, and was not of those who could defend themselves.

**c4** (28:82): The next morning, those who had wished for his place the day before said that it is God who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it, and that had God not favoured them, He would have made the earth swallow them, and that the disbelievers do not succeed.

### One-minute summary

Qarun came out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted this life wished they had what he had [c1]. Those who had been given knowledge said that the reward of God is better [c2]. God made the earth swallow him and his house [c3].

### Complete story

He came out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted the life of this world said that they wished they had what Qarun had been given, for he was possessor of a great fortune [c1]. Those who had been given knowledge said, woe to you, the reward of God is better for one who believes and does good, and none will attain it except the patient [c2]. God made the earth swallow him and his house, and he had no group to help him other than God, and was not of those who could defend themselves [c3]. The next morning, those who had wished for his place the day before said that it is God who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it, and that had God not favoured them, He would have made the earth swallow them, and that the disbelievers do not succeed [c4].

### Deep study

The passage sets groups of onlookers against each other, those who wanted the life of this world and those who had been given knowledge [c1][c2]. The next morning the first group speaks of God's extending and restricting provision [c4].

### Kids mode

Qarun came out before his people in his finery [c1]. Those who had knowledge said that the reward of God is better [c2]. God made the earth swallow him and his house [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the onlookers change their words after the earth swallows him, and speak of God as the one who extends and restricts provision [c1][c4]. Another is that the reward of God is described as better and as reached only by the patient [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the finery was, or where this took place.
- Not established: how the earth swallowed him and his house, or how long after the display.
- Not established: how many were in the groups of onlookers.

## 3. Named with Fir'awn and Haman  (`#named-with-firawn-and-haman`)

Cited ayat: 29:39-40, 40:24-25

> **29:39** وَقَٰرُونَ وَفِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ سَٰبِقِينَ
>
> **29:40** فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنۢبِهِۦ فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِبًا وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ خَسَفْنَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ أَغْرَقْنَا وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

> **40:24** إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَقَٰرُونَ فَقَالُوا۟ سَٰحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ
>
> **40:25** فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ

### Claims

**c1** (29:39): Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they could not outrun God.

**c2** (29:40): God seized each for his sin, so that against some He sent a storm of stones, some were seized by the blast, some He made the earth swallow, and some He drowned, and God did not wrong them but they wronged themselves.

**c3** (40:24): God sent Musa to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, and they said that he was a lying sorcerer.

**c4** (40:25): When he brought them the truth from God, they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women, and the plotting of the disbelievers was only in error.

### One-minute summary

Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land [c1]. They said that he was a lying sorcerer [c3]. God seized each for his sin, and the ayah lists various ways in which He did so [c2].

### Complete story

Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they could not outrun God [c1]. God seized each for his sin, so that against some He sent a storm of stones, some were seized by the blast, some He made the earth swallow, and some He drowned, and God did not wrong them but they wronged themselves [c2]. God sent Musa to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, and they said that he was a lying sorcerer [c3]. When he brought them the truth from God, they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women, and the plotting of the disbelievers was only in error [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat name Qarun together with Fir'awn and Haman [c1][c3]. The ayah that lists the ways in which God seized them does not say which fate belonged to whom [c2].

### Kids mode

Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs [c1]. They were arrogant in the land [c1]. They called Musa a lying sorcerer [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage names Qarun beside the rulers to whom Musa was sent [c1][c3]. Another is that it ends with God saying that He did not wrong them but they wronged themselves [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which of the fates in the ayah was Qarun's.
- Not established: when Qarun spoke against Musa, or in what words beyond those recorded.
